problemStatement.plain: Among all degree-$n$ polynomials with leading coefficient $1$, the one that stays closest to zero on the interval $[-1,1]$ is the (rescaled) Chebyshev polynomial, and its largest deviation is exactly $2^{-(n-1)}$. We want a formal proof of this classical extremal/minimax property.

insights: Optimality half = classical equioscillation argument: if monic p had ‖p‖∞<2^(1-n) on [-1,1], then q=Mₙ-p inherits the sign of Mₙ at the n+1 extreme nodes cos(kπ/n) (strict alternation (-1)^k·q(node)>0), giving by IVT a root strictly between each consecutive node pair = n distinct roots; but deg q < n (difference of two monic degree-n polys via degree_sub_lt), contradicting card_roots'.

Lean trick to avoid parity case-explosion in the IVT step: intermediate_value_uIcc works on the unordered interval, so with Set.mem_uIcc_of_le/_of_ge a single Nat.even_or_odd split suffices to place 0 between the two node values.

Roots are strictly interior (open intervals) because q is nonzero at the nodes themselves, so the n chosen roots are distinct via StrictAnti (node_strict_anti: cos(kπ/n) strictly decreasing in k), hence the selection map is injective.
chebyshev_minimax proves the minimax VALUE (achievability + optimality) but NOT uniqueness of the minimizer; problem.md headlines uniqueness, so uniqueness is the genuine open frontier.

Uniqueness is strictly harder than optimality: a minimizer gives only WEAK alternation of q = Mₙ - p at the n+1 nodes, so the strict-IVT root-count of monicChebyshev_minimax does not transfer; need n roots counted WITH MULTIPLICITY (Rolle/rootMultiplicity).

Crux decomposition (Rolle route, fallback): Case A — if no node is a root, weak alternation upgrades to STRICT and the verified monicChebyshev_minimax argument applies verbatim (n distinct simple interior roots vs deg<n), needing NO multiplicity. Case B — if some node is a root, that node is a non-crossing local extremum hence a root of q too (Rolle); counting roots WITH multiplicity over the n intervals still gives >=n, contradicting card_roots (<n). Only Case B is genuinely new.

UNIQUENESS crux (weak_alternation_eq_zero): a real poly q with natDegree<n that weakly alternates 0<=(-1)^k*q(x_k) at n+1 strictly-decreasing nodes must be 0. PREFERRED ROUTE = Lagrange/divided-difference (avoids Rolle/multiplicity entirely, single global argument vs Case A/B split): q = its Lagrange interpolant over range(n+1) (Lagrange.eq_interpolate); the coeff of X^n gives 0 = sum_i q(x_i)*prod_{j!=i}(x_i-x_j)^{-1}; the k-th product has sign (-1)^k (exactly k negative factors since nodes strictly decrease), so each term = (-1)^k*q(x_k)*|.| >= 0; Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg forces q(x_k)=0 for all k, giving n+1 distinct roots with deg<n, hence q=0. Strictly cleaner to formalize than the multiplicity/Rolle approach.

Uniqueness crux weak_alternation_eq_zero fully reduced via the divided-difference (Lagrange) route, avoiding the harder Rolle/multiplicity argument: q equals its own interpolant on n+1 nodes (interpolate_poly_eq_self); coeff n = n-th divided difference = sum over i of q(x_i)/prod_{j!=i}(x_i-x_j) (leadingCoeff_basis), which is 0 since deg q < n; each term is nonneg because the weight has sign (-1)^i (node_divdiff_sign) matching the weak alternation; so q vanishes at all n+1 nodes, contradicting card_roots'.
